records.title: Alraune (1930) — Illustrierter Film-Kurier, no. 1499
records.description: Illustrierter Film-Kurier Nr. 1499 — film programme for Alraune (Germany, 1930), directed by Richard Oswald, with music by Bronisław Kaper. The first sound-film adaptation of Hanns Heinz Ewers’s novel: a fanatical scientist, after creating artificial animals, fashions a synthetic human — „Alraune“ — from the bodies of a hanged man and a prostitute; the cold-hearted woman then takes cruel revenge on her „creator,“ who has fallen hopelessly in love with her. Cast: Brigitte Helm, Albert Bassermann, Harald Paulsen, Adolf E. Licho, Agnes Straub, Bernhard Goetzke. German premiere 2 March 1930 (per the Illustrierter Film-Kurier listing). Marks Kaper’s earliest film work.

records.title: Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung, 10 December 1929 — Jazz auf vier Flügeln review
records.description: Review titled 'Jazz auf vier Flügeln — Zweites städtisches Sonderkonzert in Hamborn' (signed Dr. Funk) in the Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung, 10 December 1929. It covers the First Piano Quartet (Erstes Klavier-Quartett) of four pianists — Bronisław Kaper, Leopold Mittmann, Alexander Zakin and Julian Pomeranc — performing on four grand pianos, including their own compositions. The programme ranged from Schubert, Verdi, Strauss, Kreisler and Rimsky-Korsakov to the 'Blue Danube' and modern dances; Kaper contributed a tango for four grand pianos (Vierflügeltango), and Mittmann a Jazz-Prélude and three 'Jazz-Babies'.

records.title: Hans Albers in Berlin, 1924
records.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the actor Hans Albers in a coat and hat on a Berlin street, 1924.
records.publicCaption: Hans Albers photographed walking Unter den Linden in Berlin, 1924 — nine years before he took the lead in Heut' kommt's drauf an, the 1933 comedy for which Kaper and Jurmann wrote the songs.

records.title: Marc Lavry — portrait by Helmar Lerski, 1944
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of the composer and conductor Marc Lavry, photographed by Helmar Lerski in 1944.
records.publicCaption: Marc Lavry photographed by Helmar Lerski in 1944, thirteen years after he directed the music for Seitensprünge (1931) in Berlin. Lavry conducted the Berliner Sinfonie Orchester from 1928 until the orchestra was dismantled under the National Socialist regime, and left for Riga in 1933.
records.publicCreditLine: Helmar Lerski, 1944; via the Marc Lavry Heritage Society and Wikimedia Commons.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in Israel: the Wikimedia Commons file carries the PD-Israel tag, under which copyright in a photograph made before 2008 expires fifty years after it was taken, so the term ended in 1994. That ground is Israeli, not United States law; Lerski died in 1956, so the work remains protected until 2027 in countries applying a seventy-year term from the author's death, and the United States position for a 1944 foreign photograph depends on restoration under the URAA. The photograph is dated 1944, well after the 1931 film documented here.

records.title: Alfred Piccaver — portrait, Bain News Service
records.altText: Black-and-white portrait photograph of the tenor Alfred Piccaver.
records.publicCaption: Alfred Piccaver, the English-born tenor who led the Vienna State Opera for a quarter of a century. He took the lead in Abenteuer am Lido (1933), the Austrian musical comedy scored by Kaper and Jurmann and his one substantial film role.
records.publicCreditLine: Unknown photographer, Bain News Service; Library of Congress, George Grantham Bain Collection, ggbain.34250.
records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States under the PD-US tag on the Wikimedia Commons file. The photograph comes from the Library of Congress George Grantham Bain Collection, for which the Library records no known restrictions on publication. Neither the photographer nor the exact date is established; the Commons file gives the date as unknown, and the collection's Piccaver portraits are dated by the Library between 1910 and the 1920s.

records.title: Albert Chantrier and René Nazelles — La Rampe, 1921
records.altText: Black-and-white press photograph of two men in hats and overcoats standing at a café table, reading a sheet of paper.
records.publicCaption: Albert Chantrier and René Nazelles, composer and lyricist of Le Fruit défendu, photographed for La Rampe on the operetta's run at the Théâtre Cluny. Nazelles went on to write French lyrics for Kaper.
records.publicCreditLine: Unsigned photograph, La Rampe, 9 January 1921, p. 12; Bibliothèque nationale de France, Gallica, ark:/12148/bpt6k55821649.
records.rightsNote: Public domain. Reproduced from the Bibliothèque nationale de France digitisation.

records.title: André de Badet — portrait, Gaîté-Lyrique programme, 1941
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of André de Badet in jacket and tie, facing the camera.
records.publicCaption: André de Badet, the librettist and lyricist who wrote French words for seven Kaper songs, in the author's portrait printed in the programme of his operetta L'Auberge qui chante at the Gaîté-Lyrique.

records.title: René Pujol — portrait by Henri Manuel, 1932
records.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of René Pujol in profile, wearing a suit.
records.publicCaption: René Pujol, the Bordeaux-born librettist who wrote with Charles-Louis Pothier under Albert Willemetz at the Bouffes-Parisiens, photographed by Henri Manuel for the programme of La Pouponnière.

records.publicCaption: Henry Koster, who directed Three Smart Girls in 1936, the Deanna Durbin debut that carried two songs by Kaper and Jurmann. The photograph is a later studio still, made for Flower Drum Song in 1961.

records.rightsNote: Public domain in the United States. records.title: Frank Lloyd with his Best Director award, April 1930
records.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the film director Frank Lloyd in evening dress, holding an Academy Award statuette.
records.publicCaption: Frank Lloyd at the second Academy Awards ceremony on 3 April 1930, holding the Best Director award for The Divine Lady. Five years later he directed Mutiny on the Bounty, for which Kaper wrote “Love Song of Tahiti” with Walter Jurmann and Gus Kahn.
